actions.action: Rotate dispatches across customers, not individual jobs.
actions.mechanism: Customer round-robin bounds dispatch opportunity gaps rather than optimizing mean latency or equalizing worker-seconds.
actions.implementation: Maintain one ready-ring entry per customer. Dispatch one job per turn; append new customers at the tail. Keep all twelve workers work-conserving.
actions.check: With N customers ahead of or including a waiting turn, verify dispatch within 60 × ceil(N/12) seconds, assuming transforms finish within sixty seconds.
actions.risk: Equal start counts do not imply equal compute shares.

actions.action: Limit short-job overtaking within each customer.
actions.mechanism: Prefer estimated-short jobs locally, but force FIFO service regularly so inaccurate estimates cannot permanently strand large jobs.
actions.implementation: On each customer's turns, allow two shortest-estimate selections, then select its oldest queued job. Store a per-customer modulo-three counter.
actions.check: Verify the oldest waiting job starts within three customer turns, even when new estimated-short jobs arrive continuously. Measure short-job latency separately.
actions.risk: Bad estimates reduce latency benefits; running transforms remain non-preemptible.

actions.action: Alternatively, reserve three workers for short-job opportunities.
actions.mechanism: Separate short-biased dispatch from guaranteed customer turns without preventing either group from processing long jobs.
actions.implementation: Use nine workers for customer round-robin with bounded local overtaking; three select shortest estimated jobs across all queues. Share queued jobs atomically.
actions.check: Verify customer-turn waits stay within 60 × ceil(N/9) seconds through the fair workers, including when all three short-biased workers receive underestimated long jobs.
actions.risk: This alternative weakens the twelve-worker fairness bound; reservation cannot interrupt running work.

actions.action: Correct runtime estimates using recent completion errors.
actions.mechanism: Observed runtimes improve short-job ranking; fairness remains independent of prediction accuracy and does not require accurate classification.
actions.implementation: Retain the last 100 completions with original estimates. Scale file-size estimates by their median actual-to-estimated ratio; use unchanged estimates before observations exist.
actions.check: Replay the same arrivals with corrected and uncorrected estimates. Compare prediction error and short-job latency; retain correction only if measured behavior improves.
actions.risk: A global correction can hide customer differences and lag workload changes.

actions.action: Test fairness under continuous heavy arrivals.
actions.mechanism: Adversarial replay distinguishes guaranteed service opportunities from aggregate latency improvements that can conceal starvation.
actions.implementation: Simulate twelve non-preemptive workers, one continuously backlogged sixty-second customer, and intermittent one-second customers. Underestimate long jobs and overestimate short jobs tenfold; also reverse errors.
actions.check: Record maximum customer-turn waits, oldest-job progress, short-job p95, overall mean latency, and per-customer worker-seconds. Assert the selected scheduler's bound after every dispatch.
actions.risk: Finite tests cannot prove eventual progress; document the queue-order invariant too.
